# Layer Anarchy

![Layer Anarchy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srhinos/LayerAnarchy/main/.github/hero.png)

Every layer addon on Forever runs its own network, so you only reach the hosts who use the same addon you do. The most popular one also decides when you're allowed to swap: not in combat, not while dead, not right after a fight, and only as many times an hour as the addon thinks you should.

I wanted one that talks to all of them and stays out of my way, so I made **Layer Anarchy**.

**Turn off your other layer addon first.** Layer Anarchy stays off while LayerSwap, Bulo Layer Forever, AutoLayer or another layer addon that sends or accepts invites is loaded, so the two don't fight over invites. Its window tells you which one and has a button that disables it for you.

## How it works

- **Swap** asks for an invite on LayerSwap's network (Bulo Layer Forever and Forever Simple Layer use it too), VoidNet and Forever Layer Hop at the same time, then keeps asking more players every few seconds until it finds a host or runs out of people. It takes the first invite that can move you, checks that your layer actually changed, and leaves the group.
- **AutoLayer** hosts only listen to public chat, and Forever doesn't let addons post there. After about 12 seconds an **Ask AutoLayer** button puts the request in your chat box; you press Enter to send it.
- **Hosting** is on by default for all of those networks, flight paths included. Both can be turned off.

## Going back to a layer

- Layer Anarchy recognises layers from the creatures around you, so a layer you come back to keeps its letter: *Layer B · back after 4m*. A "?" means it hasn't confirmed which layer yet. Right after you phase, nameplates blink on for a moment to read the creatures around you.
- Click the layer name for a list of the layers in your zone, when you were last on each, and the hosts known to be there. Pick one to swap straight back to it.

## Swap limits

- Nothing is blocked. Swap in combat, while dead or right after a fight.
- The game has its own hourly limit. When it refuses a move, the window tells you and counts down to when you can go again. The count comes from your own swaps, not a number I picked.
- If you want to cap how many invites you send per hour as a host, there's a slider for it, off by default.

## The window

- One status line for what's happening right now: *Hosting*, *Asking 23/59 – 1 found*, *Refused – 16 this hour*. The border colour follows it.
- **Bars:** how many players each network has, and how your swaps and hosting have gone, for the last hour or the session.
- **Cog:** options.
- **Minimize:** a small HUD.
- **Minimap button:** optional, off by default. Turn it on in the options.
- **Controller:** bind *Controller focus* to put the controller on the box.

## Commands

- `/la` shows or hides the window
- `/la swap` swaps
- `/la focus` puts the controller on the window
- `/la diag` prints a report, handy for bug reports

To swap with a key, bind **Swap layer** in the game's Keybindings, under Layer Anarchy.

## Source

GPL-3.0, written from scratch. The bundled libraries (LibStub, CallbackHandler, LibDataBroker, LibDBIcon) keep their own licences. Bugs and ideas go to [GitHub](https://github.com/srhinos/LayerAnarchy).

releases.notes:
# Layer Anarchy

## 0.2.4

- New option **Host while queued**: tick it to keep hosting while you're queued or listed in the group finder. Off by default, so hosting still pauses then.

## 0.2.3

- When you can't host right now, LayerSwap and Bulo players see you as busy or Host off, instead of "not updated".
- Hosting pauses while you're listed in the group finder, queued in the dungeon finder or queued for a battleground, so a guest joining your group can't cost you your place.

## 0.2.2

- Your chat channels keep their numbers (General 1, Trade 2 and so on), even when Layer Anarchy joins its channels first or while you're in a dungeon.
- When another layer addon is loaded, the window has a button that disables it and reloads.
- Optional minimap button, off by default: turn it on under the cog's options. Click shows or hides the window; drag it around the minimap's edge. It's a standard LibDBIcon button, so button collectors like HidingBar pick it up.

## 0.2.1

- The nameplate flash while the layer shows "?" is now a single blink half a second after you phase, instead of a second-long flash repeated every 10 seconds.

## 0.2.0

**Layers you can recognise and go back to**
- Layer letters now mean something. Layer Anarchy recognises a layer from the creatures around you, so coming back to one shows its old letter and how long you were away ("Layer B · back after 4m"). A "?" means it hasn't confirmed which layer yet; while it shows, nameplates flash on for a moment now and then to read the creatures around you.
- Click the layer name for a list of the layers in your zone, when you were last on each, and the hosts known to be there. Pick one to swap straight back to it.

**Swapping**
- Every network is asked at once, then more players every few seconds until everyone reachable has been asked. The status shows how many.
- "Ask AutoLayer" appears after about 12 seconds; "Search more" appears only when another /who needs your click.
- Swapping in combat no longer opens the Group Finder.
- Hosts on your own layer no longer count as found.
- The box resets as soon as you leave the host's group.
- Invites from friends and guildmates are left alone during a swap.

**Hosting**
- Friends who whisper "inv" or say "layer" in guild chat are no longer invited by mistake.
- Hosting no longer fills chat with group messages about strangers.
- Fixes for /reload while hosting, and for failed invites holding up your own swap.

**Also**
- Controller support: bind "Controller focus" to put the controller on the box.
- No longer switches off for LayerNumber or PartyLens.
- Many smaller fixes.

## 0.1.1

- Now on Wago.

## 0.1.0

First release.

- One-click layer swap through LayerSwap, AutoLayer, VoidNet and Forever Layer Hop at once.
- Hosts for all four networks.
- Swap in combat, while dead, whenever the game allows.
- Learns the real hourly swap limit from your own swaps and shows a reset countdown after a refusal.
- Network panel: who's on each network, your swaps and hosting, for the last hour or the session.
- Turns itself off if another layer addon is loaded.
